Delhi airport flooded, streets waterlogged after an hour of heavy rain
Heavy rain and thunderstorms lashed Delhi-NCR on Friday, triggering waterlogging at IGI Airport and disrupting flight operations. Nine flights were diverted between 3:30 pm and 4:30 pm, while the IMD forecast more rain and thunderstorms on Saturday.

Nine flights were diverted from Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport between 3:30 pm and 4:30 pm on Friday as heavy rain and thunderstorms disrupted flight operations in the national capital.
Four flights were diverted to Jaipur, four to Lucknow and one to Ahmedabad, sources said. Waterlogging was also reported at IGI Airport following the heavy rainfall.
The four flights that were diverted to Lucknow Airport on Friday were:
QP 1821: Bengaluru–Delhi, arrived at Lucknow at 4:37 pm
AI 484: Ludhiana–Delhi, arrived at 4:50 pm and departed at 5:51 pm
Delhi-NCR remained under a spell of heavy rain and thunderstorms, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issuing a red warning for heavy rainfall in parts of the region.
Delhi Airport said heavy rainfall on Friday led to water accumulation in the approach road and forecourt areas of the airport.
The airport authorities said the accumulated water was cleared shortly after, adding that efforts were underway to ensure smooth airport operations.
Heavy rain also lashed several parts of West Delhi. The downpour led to waterlogging in many areas, including Gandhi Market in Sagarpur.
Roads in quite a few residential colonies were submerged, turning them into waterlogged stretches.
However, there have been no reports of waterlogging on major roads or traffic jams so far.
According to the Regional Meteorological Centre, New Delhi, Palam recorded the highest rainfall of 72.2 mm between 2:30 pm and 5:30 pm.
During the same period, Narayana recorded 54 mm, followed by Janakpuri at 48.5 mm, Lodhi Road at 34.6 mm and Safdarjung at 32.6 mm.
Other areas also received significant rainfall, with Pusa recording 29 mm, Jharoda Kalan 25 mm, Ridge 20 mm, Chhatarpur 15 mm and Ayanagar 12 mm.
According to the weather department's 5:40 pm bulletin, rain continued across several parts of Delhi. The 72.2 mm recorded in Palam over three hours was the highest rainfall recorded in the capital during the period.
With rain continuing to fall heavily, prolonged showers could worsen waterlogging and cause traffic disruptions across parts of West Delhi.
A squall was reported at Delhi’s Palam Airport on Friday, with gusty winds reaching 76 kmph, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).
The squall occurred between 3:37 pm and 3:39 pm IST and lasted around two minutes. During the spell, humidity rose by four percentage points from 86% to 90%, while the temperature fell by 0.5°C from 26°C to 25.5°C.
UNTIL WHEN WILL HEAVY RAIN LAST?
Delhi began the day under generally cloudy skies, and the weather is expected to remain unsettled through the day.
At Safdarjung, the IMD has forecast a maximum temperature of around 32°C on Friday, with moderate rain likely. The local forecast also points to thunderstorms with lightning and moderate to heavy rainfall during the afternoon.
The IMD has forecast another day of heavy rain over the Haryana-Chandigarh-Delhi region on Saturday, September 5.
Delhi's local forecast also indicates moderate rain, with thunderstorms and lightning through different parts of the day.
The warning is also relevant for the wider NCR.
West Uttar Pradesh, which includes several NCR areas, is under a heavy-rain warning on September 4 and 5, according to the IMD.
WHY IS IT RAINING SO HEAVILY IN DELHI?
The current spell is linked to an active monsoon weather system over north-central India. IMD has said a well-marked low-pressure area over northeast Madhya Pradesh and adjoining areas is producing significant rainfall over parts of central India.
The system is expected to influence weather conditions as it persists over the region.
For Delhi-NCR, the immediate outlook is therefore one of continued clouds, rain and thunderstorms through Saturday.
The intensity is expected to ease after that, with the IMD currently showing no heavy-rain warning for the Delhi subdivision from September 6 onward, although light rain or drizzle could still occur.
